Hold a threshold lookup table between absolute bounds

Source: R/bound_threshold.R
bound_threshold.Rd

Raises a threshold to min where it falls below it, and lowers it to max where it rises above it, leaving the rest untouched. The bound is recorded on each threshold so that the flag, the excess and the label all describe the threshold actually used.

Usage

bound_threshold(x, min = NULL, max = NULL, cols = NULL)

Arguments

x

A threshold lookup table, from calc_percentile() or built by the user, with registered threshold columns.

min, max

Bounds in the data's unit: the threshold is held at or above min and at or below max. One number, or one for each column bounded.

cols

<tidy-select> Columns to bound; by default every registered threshold column, the whole-year ones included.

Value

x with the chosen columns bounded. A registered threshold also records min_threshold and max_threshold on its entry, so the label and the excess follow; a column named through cols that the registry does not know is bounded without one being invented for it.

Details

This combines a relative threshold with an absolute guardrail, which is what makes one definition of an extreme travel across climates: the 95th percentile of a mild month is not a hot day anywhere, and a fixed level alone fires every year in the tropics and never in the highlands. Passing both conditions is the same as passing the harder of the two, so a single bounded threshold replaces a hand-written day_abv_99p & day_abv_30.

Thresholds are lookup tables whoever produced them, so this works on a table from calc_percentile() and equally on agro-ecological zone limits, per-district thresholds or crop-specific limits supplied by the user.

Give min for an upper threshold and max for a lower one, so that the bound points the same way as the tail. The other pairing widens the indicator instead of narrowing it, and is warned about. Where the bound governs, the exceedance rate is no longer the nominal one; that is the point of giving it.

See also

calc_percentile(), calc_threshold_day()

Other indicators: calc_anomaly(), calc_condition(), calc_heatwave(), calc_par(), calc_percentile(), calc_percentile_day(), calc_spell(), calc_spell_excess(), calc_spell_percentile(), calc_std_index(), calc_std_threshold(), calc_threshold_day()

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e")
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pct <- calc_percentile(extracted, p = c(0.95, 0.99))

# A hot day is unusual for the place and month AND at least 25 C.
bound_threshold(pct, min = 25)
} # }
